keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Republic was proclaimed on 14 April 1931 but Cliopatria's row starts in 1932; same cells as the 1932 shape. The infobox gives no area.
854,092 km2 (the page gives no area to compare): Spain with Spanish Morocco, the Sahara, Ifni and Guinea. The pages opened do not date or name the colonial territories, so the shape stands.

correction.text: the 1936 shape without Spanish Morocco and the Canary Islands (the 1936 shape already leaves out 17 of the 19 Balearic cells and keeps two, probably Menorca, which the page does not name)

keyframe_review.note: 647,124 km2: Cliopatria cuts the Nationalist mainland (789 cells, with most of the Balearics) but keeps Spanish Morocco, the Canaries, the Sahara and Guinea, although the page puts Spanish Morocco, the Canary and the Balearic islands in Nationalist hands in July 1936. The page is silent on Spanish Guinea, the Sahara and Ifni, which the shape keeps (a gap-filler should open Spanish Sahara and Spanish Guinea). The shape covers 1936-1937; the northern coast falls in 1937 (ledger).

correction.text: unchanged for 1938; 1939 is the new keyframe

keyframe_review.note: 515,454 km2: the shape stops in 1938 but the Republic lasted until 1 April 1939; Barcelona fell 'in early 1939' and Madrid in March. The 1938 shape holds for 1938; 1939 is the new keyframe.
New keyframe: the Republic after the fall of Catalonia (early 1939) until the dissolution of 1 April 1939.

ledger.note: 1931: the Second Spanish Republic is proclaimed on 14 April 1931 (infobox); the page names no territory, so the core is Cliopatria's 1932 shape: Spain with its Moroccan, Saharan and Guinean possessions.
1936: the rising reaches Spanish Morocco on 18 July 1936 and mainland Spain a day later; Spanish Morocco is Nationalist ('control all but certain').

1936: 'Franco and Goded took control of the Canary and Balearic islands to which they were assigned'; the page does not say which Balearic islands (Menorca is not named). [Reviewer eu-21-c, 2026-10-31: confidence 3 lowered to 2: the page says only that Goded and Franco took control of the islands to which they were assigned and names no Balearic island; Menorca stayed Republican (the 1936 keyframe keeps two Balearic cells)]

region.text: the Nationalist zone of July-October 1936, as Cliopatria's 1936 shape cuts it from the 1932 shape

ledger.note: 1936: the rising holds Seville, Cadiz, Old Castile, Leon and Galicia while the government keeps Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Malaga, Jaen, Almeria, most of the east coast, Asturias, Cantabria and part of the Basque Country; by October 1936 the rebels held 'much of the south and west' (Second Republic page). Region from Cliopatria's own 1936 cut.
1936: the government moves from Madrid to Valencia on 6 November 1936 as Madrid is under siege.
1937: the Nationalist northern campaign; 'the Nationalists captured most of Spain's northern coastline in 1937' (the page gives no months).
1937: the northern coast is in Nationalist hands by the end of the year (page gives no months).
1937: the north falls to the Nationalists (page: most of the northern coastline captured in 1937; no month for the Basque Country, Santander or Asturias).
1937: the government moves from Valencia to Barcelona on 31 October 1937.

region.text: the land the 1938 shape lacks that the 1936 shape had (Cliopatria)

ledger.note: 1938: the remaining Nationalist gains between Cliopatria's 1936 and 1938 shapes (Aragon, the push to the Mediterranean, the south-east). The page opened is silent on the Aragon offensive of April 1938 and the Ebro battle; the region is the shape difference, not a source's wording.
1938: the Nationalist attack on Catalonia; the page says much of Catalonia was captured 'in 1938 and 1939' without dates for the offensive.
1939: Barcelona 'fell to the rebels in early 1939' (Second Republic page; no day).
1939: Catalonia falls; Barcelona 'fell to the rebels in early 1939'.

region.text: the central and south-eastern zone around Madrid, Valencia and Murcia

ledger.note: 1939: the Republican remainder collapses. Colonel Casado leads a coup against the government on 5 March 1939; Franco enters Madrid in March and 'declared victory on 1 April 1939'.
1939: the Republic 'was dissolved on 1 April 1939' after surrendering in the civil war; its government survived in exile and kept an embassy in Mexico City until 1976.

wars.name: Spanish Civil War
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: the rising of 17-19 July 1936; Franco enters Madrid and declares victory on 1 April 1939; the Republic is dissolved the same day.
wars.note: Foreign intervention is not on the extract read; the page gives few months: northern campaign 1937, Catalonia 1938-1939.

certainty.note: Spain's frontiers and the Moroccan protectorate; the Sahara and Guinea limits are not described on the pages opened.
Front lines; the pages give no monthly line.

notes: Page budget (2 pages) spent on the Second Spanish Republic and Spanish Civil War articles, both thin on dates: no months for the northern campaign, the Aragon offensive, the Ebro or the Catalonia offensive, and silent on Spanish Guinea, Spanish Sahara and Ifni (kept inside the 1936 shape). The 1938 aggregate loss event is confidence 1. The kept-in Canary/Moroccan lands mean the Cliopatria 1936 and 1938 shapes over-state the Republic. Counterpart spanish-nationalists is a Cliopatria row (1936-1938) written by another part. Ends 1 April 1939 where Cliopatria stops in 1938.
